design_decisions: The new interpreter test for spawns written directly in a sim.run body is its own file, sim_tasks.wf, instead of a case in sim.wf. This way the CLI test that counts passed tests in sim.wf does not change.

W0313 tracks capabilities on values (Val.caps) and locals (Local.caps). A struct or container owned by a local of the handled body can hold the closure without an error. A value that is stored behind a reference, or given to unknown or storing code, counts as an escape (sound side). Passing to an operation or a resume counts only for the capabilities of handlers inside the receiving clause.

The suspension-point rule is written as spec rules that derive multi_at (input facts clause_multi, body_multi, resumes_at). It is not hidden in fact generation, so --explain shows it. A resume counts as multi if any clause of its handler is multi (conservative).

F6: forwards(H) is derived from clause_performs(H, E). The input forwards(H) now marks only the root handlers of sim.run, which W0802 covers. HandlerInfo keeps its field name, which keeps the merge with review/quality small.

Effect identity: canonical() returns identities, and effect_named falls back to an identity lookup. This way the interpreter's effect resolution works without changes. EffectDef.name stays the written name for display.

A call of a function parameter or an unknown function value can start a task with its function argument, so W0314 checks that argument (sound). Corpus markers record the extra W0314 on to_parameter and unknown_spawner.
Authority (W0901) counts only standard effects. A user effect of a dependency needs a handler from the caller, not authority.
Pub enforcement uses W0101 ('is private'), not a new code. It applies only across units, and functions in the prelude are exempt.

issues.finding: RT12 missed shape: a spawning closure that a callee or a function value calls more than once
issues.description: apply_summary emits spawned_at(T, n) once, at the call node. Nothing models a callee that calls its fn parameter in a loop or twice. So several copies of the task write the same place at the same time, and no W0405 is reported. When the loop is written in place, W0405 is reported (the task conflicts with itself at its second spawn node). The common for-each shape is unsound: `each(v, |x| { s.spawn(|| st.count += x); () })`.
issues.repro: P=SCRATCH/verify/partb/S3/p; $P/../weft check $P/r12e.wf: per_item (line 6, each(...)) and twice_value (line 20, g(sp) where g = |f: fn()| { f(); f() }) give 0 errors. issues.suggested_fix: When a summary that has spawns runs through a callee parameter, a passthrough or an unknown value (apply_value, call_param, call_unknown), count each of its tasks as possibly started more than once. For example, make the task active at the call node itself, so that the task conflicts with its own writes there. Add bad and clean corpus cases in 61_task_paths.wf.

issues.finding: Effect identity: the interpreter resolves `handle log` to a user effect named Log
issues.description: The checker accepts `handle log { fn info(m) {..} }` as a handler of the standard Log in a module that defines a user `Log` (64_effect_names.wf handled_std). The interpreter's compile.rs effect_of works differently: canonical(m, "log") gives "Log", and effect_named(m, "Log") calls lookup first, which finds the user Log. The `info` clause is then skipped, and `log.info` goes to the root handler. So the checker and the interpreter disagree: a standard effect that the checker counts as handled is performed on the root. The report says that the interpreter needed no changes, but this case does need one.

issues.suggested_fix: In weft-interp compile.rs effect_of and path_ref, resolve the identity from effects::canonical with effects::by_identity. Or make Program::effect_named prefer by_identity when the name is an identity of a standard effect. Add an interpreter program with main that handles `log` in a module that shadows Log.

issues.finding: RT12 false W0405: a closure that only defines or returns a spawning closure counts as spawning
issues.description: spawn() adds the task to every barrier frame between the scope binder and the spawn. So an outer closure that defines an inner spawning closure, and does not call it, starts the task at each of its own calls. A factory closure starts the task twice: once at mk() and once at g().
issues.repro: P=SCRATCH/verify/partb/S3/p; weft check $P/r12b.wf: not_called_inner gives W0405 at line 38, but `b` is never called. weft check $P/r12a.wf: returned gives W0405 at line 38 (`g()`).

So does `r.add(|| log("x"))`, where r is a struct local to the body and add pushes into self. A direct `v.push(..)` on a local Vec is accepted, so the results are not consistent. ADR 0005 lists 'a callee that stores it or has no body' as imprecision, so this is documented. Box.new is the clearest case.

issues.finding: W0313 misses a closure given to an operation of its own handler (rule 6: a clause runs outside its handler)
issues.description: perform_op calls keep_for_op(&v, at) with at = index of the operation's handler, and keep_for_op skips handlers up to and including at. So the capability of the receiving handler H counts as live in H's clause. It is not: H's clause runs in the handle-site environment, with H removed (expr.rs pops H before it lowers the clauses). A clause that calls or returns the argument then performs through a dead capability. The checker accepts and the interpreter fails. This is an off-by-one in crates/weft-sema/src/body/call.rs perform_op (the `let at = self.handlers.iter().rposition(..); self.keep_for_op(&v, at)` lines).
issues.repro: Probes in SCRATCH/verify/partb/p/: a1_same_handler.wf (`handle Reg { fn reg(g) { g(); resume(()) } fn ping() {..} } in reg(|| ping())`) and a4_get_own.wf (`handle Get { fn get(g) { g } } in get(|| { let x = get(|| print(2)) })`). For both, `weft check` reports 0 errors, and `weft run` gives 'runtime error: no handler for `Reg.ping` / `Get.get` on this task'. The base also accepted them.
issues.suggested_fix: Count the receiving handler as inside the clause: pass at.and_then(|i| i.checked_sub(1)) (as resume does with depth-1), or skip(at) for operations. Add a bad case (own operation) and a clean case (inner_operation already covers the outer one) to 62_cap_escape.wf.

issues.finding: W0313 misses a capability that leaves through a resume argument and the operation result
issues.description: keep_for_op at resume checks only the handlers inside the clause. But the resumed body gets the value as the result of its operation, and perform_op returns Val { ty: o.ret } with no caps. So a clause of an inner handle can resume with a closure that performs through an outer local handler. The body returns it as the handle value, and the outer handler's check_cap_escape does not see it. This is rule 6, which the stage claimed (63 resume_escapes covers only handlers inside the clause).
issues.repro: p/g3_resume_leak.wf: `handle Log {..} in { handle Get { fn get() { resume(|| log("late")) } } in get() }` returned from leak(), then called in main. `weft check` gives 0 errors, and `weft run` gives 'no handler for `Log.log` on this task'.
issues.suggested_fix: Give an operation result whose type holds function values the caps of every local handler outside the receiving handler. A resume argument can only carry those caps. Or collect the caps of the resume arguments per capability and join them into the handle value and into the op result. Add bad and clean corpus cases.

issues.finding: Interpreter resolves `handle log` to a user effect named Log (shadowing regression)
issues.description: Sema now resolves the canonical identity with effects::by_identity. But the interpreter's compile.rs effect_of still calls prog.effect_named(m, &names[0]), and effect_named does a lookup in module m first. So in a module that defines `effect Log`, the standard identity "Log" resolves to the user effect. The interpreter installs the handler for the wrong effect, and log.info goes to the runtime. find_op (compile.rs:365) has the same pattern. The checker and the interpreter now disagree. The base rejected the program (W0104), so this is a regression of the claimed 'interpreter works without changes'. No interpreter test covers shadowing.
issues.repro: p/d2b.wf (`// weft: no-runtime`, `effect Log {..}`, `handle log { fn info(m) { resume(()) } } in { log.info("y") }`): base gives W0104, HEAD gives 0 errors, and `weft run` gives 'no runtime: nothing handles `Log.info`'. In p/d1_shadow_interp.wf the clause never runs: the output is 'info: y' and not 'caught y'.
issues.suggested_fix: In weft-interp compile.rs effect_of, use weft_sema::effects::by_identity on the canonical identities, as sema does. Check find_op's effect_named(m, &e.name) comparison the same way. Add an interpreter program with a shadowing `effect Log`, `handle log` and `handle Log`.

issues.finding: W0313 misses a closure that a callee returns inside a tuple
issues.description: call_fn tracks a function argument only through `stores` or through a Ty::Fn result (sig.effects.ret). A function-typed argument that comes back inside a tuple (or another non-Fn result that holds functions) gets no caps on `out`. kept_vals covers only non-Fn parameters. A struct result is caught only because the callee 'stores' it.

Through a call it is not covered: worker() forks or spawns a branch that performs `log`, and the caller installs `handle log` around the call. design_decisions: Type properties come from one table per definition: Program.props, a OnceLock<TypeProps> in the new crates/weft-sema/src/props.rs. For each definition it holds an always flag and the type parameters that pass the property on, computed as a least fixpoint. Recursive types are not plain data. Pointer types (Box, Rc) do not pass !Move on. Recorded in ADR 0007.

New spec input relations: overwrites(V,P), a new value of a part drops the old one, and unset_at(V,P), a declaration with no value. New sink use_before_set(V,P), code W0304. The checker mirrors both in rules.rs (linear() and unset()), and the random generator covers them.
W0120 (non-exhaustive match) is a sema diagnostic, like the other pattern and type checks. ADR 0002 lists it.

A linear closure given to a function parameter is W0601: the callee can drop it. with_timeout is the exception, because it runs its block once. A once closure moves at the call, and a second move (W0502) follows if the callee can call it more than once, or if an operation gets it. A once closure cannot go into a place of plain data (W0502). Recorded in ADR 0007, and the imprecision is listed.

New inferred signature part EffectSig.drops: by-value parameters of a type parameter that some path of the body does not move. A caller that gives a linear value there gets W0601. It also follows a T that the body gives on to another dropping callee. infer.rs compares and copies it with the other parts.

By-value parameters that hold references (Option<&T>, generic structs of refs) get a Param root. Callers substitute the argument places for them. A new value of the parameter itself stays local and is filtered out of the signature (ADR 0003).

A call result with an unstated reference points anywhere inside the ref-typed arguments (wildcard). Type parameters pass the values of by-value arguments on exactly, and held references flow too. Stated places such as `&T in self[]` stay exact. Top-level and tuple-part references must still state their place (W0204). Nested ones may state it (`Option<&T in v[]>`) or not.
W0605 stays about written reference fields. Generic instances such as Option<&T>, Vec<&T> and Wrap<&T> can hold references, and the facts follow their places (ADR 0003).

Open and recorded: references stored behind a reference parameter (ADR 0003); operation results that hold references (ADR 0005); generic callees that abort or are multi while they hold a linear T, and a Vec of linear values has no consumer (ADR 0007).

issues.finding: RT8/RT14: a closure given to a type-parameter parameter skips every mode check (Vec.push, generic callees)
issues.description:
In call_fn (crates/weft-sema/src/body/call.rs, about line 474), the guard `if !matches!(self.inf.shallow(&pt), Ty::Fn(_)) || av.val.summary.is_none()` skips keep_modes, the `drops` check and consume when a parameter `x: T` is instantiated to a closure type. `if !callback(i) { continue; }` also skips give_fn, because T is not a function type. So the closure is never moved and never checked. Four results:
(a) A once closure in an annotated Vec<fn()> can be called twice. The program checks with 0 errors, and the interpreter faults with 'a value is used after it was moved'.
(b) A linear closure pushed into Vec<fn()> goes away silently: 0 errors and no rollback. ADR 0007 says a Vec<fn()> cannot hold a linear closure.
(c) `gen_drop(|| rollback(tx))`, with `fn gen_drop<T>(x: T) {}`, gives 0 errors.
(d) False positive: `let f = || rollback(tx); let g = gen_keep(f); g()` gives W0601 on f, although g runs the closure. Base gave nothing.
The same named-closure path lets `v.push(f); f()` call f again after the push.
issues.repro:
Probes in SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4/:
- run/vec_fn_run.wf: `let v: Vec<fn()> = Vec.new(); v.push(|| rollback(tx)); let g = v[0]; let h = v[0]; g(); h()`. Check gives 0 errors; `weft run` prints 'rollback 1', then a runtime error at 9:24.
- run/gen3.wf g2: `v.push(f); f(); let g = v[0]; g()` gives 0 errors, then a runtime fault.
- run/vec_fn_drop.wf gives 0 errors.
- p/c2_generic_drop.wf line 15 has no diagnostic.
- p/c4_generic_clean.wf line 11 gives a false W0601.
issues.suggested_fix: Handle a closure value at a parameter that is not a callback like any other by-value argument: move it (move_var), apply `drops`, and run keep_modes against the declared element or parameter type. A once closure must not go into a container of plain data such as Vec<fn()>, where an element read copies it. A linear closure there must be W0601. Add Vec<fn()> and generic T cases to corpus 71 and 72.

issues.finding: RT14: the generic `drops` part sees only direct non-moves of the parameter; a move into something that is then dropped hides the drop
issues.description:
param_drops (body/drops.rs) puts a parameter in `drops` only if some path does not move the parameter variable itself. If the body moves T into a local, a struct, an Option, a Vec, a tuple, a closure or a closure parameter, and that holder is dropped, nothing is reported. The body does not know that T is linear, and `drops` sees a move.
An overwrite of a T place inside a generic body also drops the old value silently: `self.x = y` in `impl<T> Wrap<T>`, and `w.x = y` through `&Wrap<T>`. This is the generic form of RT14's `p.tx = begin()`.
ADR 0007 does not list either shape as open.
issues.repro:
Files in SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4/:
- run/drops3.wf: `fn d9<T>(x: T) { let y = x }` and `fn d5<T>(x: T) { let o = Some(x) }`, called with begin(). Check gives 0 errors. `weft run` prints 'done' with no rollback.
- run/drops2.wf: c4 (Wrap{x:x}), c5, c6 (v.push(x)), c7, c8 (`let _ = x`), c9, c11 (`match Some(x) { Some(_) => .. }`), c12 (closure) and c15 (closure param) all give 0 errors.
- run/gen_set.wf: s1 `w.set(mk(2))` and s2 `put(&w, mk(2))` give 0 errors and print only 'rollback 2' twice, so Tx 1 is lost.
issues.suggested_fix: Compute `drops` from the facts of the generic body: treat each value whose type mentions a type parameter as linear for this analysis, and report the parameter if any such value reaches a scope_end or an overwrite while live. Or list these shapes as open in ADR 0007.

issues.finding: New false positive: a generic function that returns T through an if/match tail gets drops={x}
issues.description: `fn keep3<T>(x: T, c: bool) -> T { if c { x } else { x } }` puts x in `drops`, so every caller that gives it a linear value gets W0601. The same happens with match tails, and with mutual recursion that ends in `else { x }`. Base gave no error. The cause is the pre-existing bug in the next issue: an arm tail that names a local records no moved_at. param_drops then finds a path on which x does not move.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4/p/g4_iftail.wf: c3 `rollback(keep3(begin(), true))` gives W0601 at line 6, and c6 (match) at line 12. Base: 0. p/g3_mutual.wf c2 (keep/keep2) gives W0601 at line 10.
issues.suggested_fix: Make an if/match arm tail that names a local move that local (see the next issue). Then these cases go away.

issues.finding: Pre-existing, in RT14/RT15 scope: a local named as an if/match arm tail is not moved (use after move, !Move moves, linear false positives)
issues.description:
`let x = if c { a } else { b }` records no moved_at for a or b. A block `{ a }` does record it. Three results:
- `eat(a)` after the if gives no W0302. This is unsound.
- A !Move a or b moves with no W0604, also inside `keep_o(if c { a } else { b })`.
- Linear a and b get a false W0601 after `rollback(x)`.
Base behaves the same. S4 claims !Move transitivity and linear drops in every shape, and the bug now also causes the new `drops` false positive above.
issues.repro:
Files in SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4/:
- p/i4_if_move2.wf a(): no W0302 at line 5. b() with a block gives W0302.
- p/i2_immovable_expr.wf: j01, j03 and j04 have no W0604.
- p/i3_if_move.wf: a() gives a false W0601 for a and b at line 8. b() reads a.n after the move with no error.
issues.suggested_fix: In if_expr and match_expr, consume the arm's tail value when the result is used by value, as the block path does.

issues.finding: New false positive from the Lower::finish flag recompute: an untyped closure parameter that moves into a local
issues.description: While a local's type is still an inference variable, a move of it counts as a copy: ty_has(Var, NotCopy) is false, so no moved_at is recorded. Lower::finish then marks the local linear from its resolved type, and the missing move turns into a false W0601. Untyped closure parameters are a common shape. Base gave 0 errors.
issues.repro:
SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4/run/late.wf:
- l1 `let f = |y| { let z = y
 rollback(z) }; f(begin())` gives W0601 'linear value `y` is dropped' at line 7.
- l5 `|y| { let z = y
 z }` gives W0601 for y and z.
Base: 0 errors for both.

issues.finding: RT8: nonportable and not-many (uniq) modes are lost through plain-data places and containers
issues.description:
keep_modes covers linear closures (W0601) and once closures (W0502) that go into a place of type fn(). It does not cover nonportable or uniq captures.
- A closure that captures an Rc goes into `Cb { f: fn() }`, `cb.f = ..` or an annotated Vec<fn()>, then into a fork: no W0401.
- A closure that captures a `@ uniq` part goes into a fn() field, a tuple or an Option and stays live across a multi operation: no W0503.
Only the bare closure local is caught. Nonportable through a tuple and an Option is caught.
issues.repro:
Files in SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4/:
- p/c6_field_launder.wf: vec_fn (line 10), uniq_field (line 16) and assign_field (line 26) give 0 errors.
- p/c5_nonportable.wf: field_closure (line 36) gives 0 errors.
- p/u2_closure_uniq.wf: u2 (tuple) and u3 (Option) give no W0503. u1 is caught.
issues.suggested_fix: In keep_modes, also reject a nonportable closure in a place whose type is portable. Carry not-many as a type property (or through the value's caps) for tuples, Option and fields, as Linear and Nonportable are carried.

issues.finding: RT15: W0304 for unset place fields misses closures, nested literals and call results
issues.repro:
Files in SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4/:
- run/unset_closure.wf: s06 `let c = || print(f.cur); c()`, s07 and s08 give 0 errors. `weft run` prints `<moved>`.
- run/unset_ret.wf: s01 (mk()) and s03 (nested literal) give 0 errors and print `<moved>` twice.
- p/i5_selfref.wf s06 gives 0 errors.
issues.suggested_fix: Count a closure capture of the struct as a use of its unset field variables. Make unset variables for nested literals. For values from callees, treat a place field of a returned !Move value as unset, or require that a literal with a place field is built only where it is bound.

issues.finding: RT24/W0120: when the step budget runs out, a non-exhaustive match is accepted silently
issues.description:
exhaust.rs returns true from covers() when the 20 000-step BUDGET runs out, and check_exhaustive then reports nothing. Two things make the budget easy to reach:
- covers() still splits a column while any row has a constructor in it, also when an earlier row is all wildcards;
- it tries `true` before `false`.
So a 16-column bool tuple with one arm per column, `(..true at i..)`, that misses the all-false case is accepted. The same match with 10 columns is reported. The W0120 text says the interpreter stops if no arm matches, so a checked program can fault at runtime. No ADR records the budget.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4/p/x_bools16.wf gives 0 errors. p/x_bools10.wf, the same shape with 10 columns, gives W0120.
issues.suggested_fix: When the budget runs out, report W0120 (or a 'match too large to check' error) instead of accepting. Return true as soon as a row has only wildcards, so this shape costs linear time. Record the decision in ADR 0002.

issues.finding: Performance regression: var_has scans all locals for each query, so Lower::finish is quadratic
issues.description:
Lower::var_has (body/mod.rs:1296) runs `self.locals.iter().filter(|l| l.var == v)` for each query. finish calls local_has for each local, so the cost is O(locals^2).
- 6000 distinct `let iK = 1` take 5.9 s on head against 0.29 s on base (debug).
- verify/le_15000.wf takes 35.2 s against 1.7 s. At 3000 statements it is 1.44 s against 0.12 s.
gdb samples show finish, then local_has, then var_has. A base vs head comparison with a 60 s timeout lost W0601 on the long_explain, le_10000 and le_15000 programs. The quality review counts this kind of hot path as a regression (QR8, QR9, QR14).
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4/p/q8_distinct.wf (6000 lets): `time weft check`. Also SCRATCH/verify/le_15000.wf.
issues.suggested_fix: Index the locals by VarId once, for example a Vec<Vec<usize>> built before finish, or cache local_has for each var.

issues.finding: Pre-existing false positive: a closure that returns a linear value gets W0601 at its body
issues.description:
`let f = || begin(); rollback(f())`, `|| { let t = begin()
 t }`, `|| Some(begin())` and `apply(|| begin())`, with `apply(g: fn() -> Tx) -> Tx`, all give W0601 'temporary is dropped' at the closure. Base does the same. It is in RT14's area, and no ADR records it.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4/p/d3_closure_ret.wf gives W0601 at lines 6, 10, 15 and 20. p/d2_clean.wf c13 gives W0601 at line 40.
issues.suggested_fix: Treat the closure tail value as moved to the closure's return, as a function tail is.

issues.finding: Overwriting None is 'overwritten', now also for unannotated locals
issues.description:
`let o = None
 o = Some(begin())`, then a match that consumes o, gives 'o is overwritten before it is consumed'. The annotated form did this in base. The finish recompute extends it to the common inferred form. ADR 0007 lists the None imprecision only for `drops`.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4/p/v2_none.wf: inferred() gives W0601 at line 9. Base: 0.
issues.suggested_fix: Do not report an overwrite of a local whose only value on each path is a constructor with no linear part. Or add this case to the ADR 0007 imprecisions.

issues.finding: !Move edge cases: Box.new(Frame{..}) is W0604, and Weak<T> passes !Move on
issues.description: Box.new takes `x: T`, so a !Move literal there now gives W0604. No code can then build a Box<Frame>, although corpus 73 uses Box<Frame> and the design says !Move values are built in place. Base accepted it. Weak is an extern type with no deref and no elem, so eval_adt lets it pass Immovable on, although Weak is a pointer.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4/p/i1_immovable.wf i19 gives W0604 at line 49.
issues.suggested_fix: Build a !Move argument of Box.new and Rc.new in place. Mark Weak as a pointer in the prelude, or treat any extern without an elem step as a pointer.

issues.finding: Adjacent RT8 shape: a reference to a nonportable value is portable
issues.description: ty_has(Ref(x), Nonportable) is false. So `let r = &n` with n: Rc, then `fork(|| r.clone(), || r.clone())`, is accepted: redteam t02 rc_by_ref. A closure that captures r is accepted too. Base does the same.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/redteam/t02_fork.wf lines 14-18 and SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4/p/c5_nonportable.wf ref_to_rc both give 0 errors.
issues.suggested_fix: Let Nonportable pass through Ty::Ref, or record that this is out of scope in ADR 0006.

I verified S4 on review/s3 (353099e..3b1df44) in /home/user/wt-core. I did not edit the worktree, it is clean, and I deleted my base build.

**Gates:** cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace (also the weft-interp programs), random agreement at 5000 cases and `weft agree` on all new corpus files and probes all pass. The doc gate fails on weft-syntax and weft-check on both base and head, so the failure is not new.

**Probes:** every listed review probe gives its expected diagnostic on the right line. I wrote about 300 adversarial variants under SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4/p and .../run. Most fixes hold: RT3 reference flow, RT14 drops and overwrites, RT15 !Move transitivity and W0605, RT18/RT24 uniq, F5, definite assignment, exhaustiveness, QR7/QR8 performance and QR12.

Remaining problems: 1 blocker, 8 major, 5 minor.

**Blocker:** a closure given to a type-parameter parameter (Vec.push, generic callees) is never moved and never mode-checked. A once closure in a Vec<fn()> can be called twice: the program checks with 0 errors and the interpreter faults. A linear closure pushed into a Vec<fn()> goes away silently, although ADR 0007 says it cannot. `gen_drop(|| rollback(tx))` is accepted. There is also a new false positive: `let g = gen_keep(f); g()` gives W0601 on f.

**Major:**
- The generic `drops` part misses `let y = x`, `Some(x)`, a struct, `v.push(x)`, closures, and an overwrite of a T place in a generic body. The interpreter shows linear values lost.
- New false positive: a generic function that returns T through an if/match tail gets W0601 at each caller. The cause is a pre-existing bug: a local named as an if/match tail is not moved. That bug also misses W0302 and W0604, and gives linear false positives.
- New false positive from the finish recompute: an untyped closure parameter that moves into a local gets W0601.
- Nonportable and uniq closure modes are lost through fn() fields, Vec<fn()>, tuples and Option.
- W0304 for unset place fields misses closures, nested literals and call results. The interpreter reads `<moved>`.
- When the W0120 step budget runs out, a non-exhaustive match is accepted silently. No ADR records this.
- Lower::finish is quadratic in the number of locals: 35 s against 1.7 s on 15000 statements.

issues.finding: Generic `drops` only sees params that are never moved; a T moved into a value that is then dropped slips through
issues.description: param_drops (body/drops.rs) puts a T param in `drops` only when some path from entry to exit has no moved_at of the param. Inside a generic body T is not linear, so moving x into something that then goes away silently counts as a consume. drop_linear, wild_drops, overwrites and keep_modes all test is_linear(T), which is false. Callers that give a linear value lose it with no W0601. ADR 0007 does not list these shapes as open; it lists only abort and multi inside generic callees. Base misses them too, but this stage adds `drops` and the W0601 text 'A generic function can drop a value of a type parameter'.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4diff/p/gen1.wf. Each of these gives 0 W0601 at the caller: `fn wrap_drop<T>(x: T) { let o = Some(x) }`, `fn tuple_drop<T>(x: T) { let p = (x, 1) }`, `fn closure_drop<T>(x: T) { let c = || { let y = x } }`, `fn let_wild<T>(x: T) { let _ = x }`, `fn overwrite<T>(x: T, y: T) -> T { let z = x; z = y; z }`, `fn vec_drop<T>(x: T) { let v = Vec.new(); v.push(x) }`, each called with begin(). Only `two<T>(x, y) -> T { x }` is caught.
issues.suggested_fix: Compute drops with T treated as 'maybe linear': lower the generic body with is_linear(Ty::Param) true for the drop and overwrite paths (drop_linear, wild_drops, assign overwrites, keep_modes, closure linearity). Then put i in drops if the var of param i, or any hidden var that its value flows into, reaches a scope_end or overwrite node while live. Add bad and clean cases to 72_linear_drops.wf.

issues.finding: Local.uniq after if/else or match depends on lowering order (RT24 sticky uniq still slips through)
issues.description: assign_local sets `self.locals[l].uniq = v.uniq`. This is lowering state, not a join over paths. After `if c { l = &w[] } else { l = r }` the else branch is lowered last, so l counts as @ uniq and needs_uniq(l) is accepted. On the then path an aliased reference goes to an @ uniq parameter. The same happens with match arms. A one-armed if is caught only because the then branch is lowered last.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4diff/p/uniq1.wf: branch_alias (line 5) and match_alias (line 22) give no W0406. branch_alias2 and loop_alias are caught.
issues.suggested_fix: Save Local.uniq before the branches of if, match and handle, and at the join set it to the AND over the incoming branches, as other per-local lowering state does at joins. Or derive uniq at the use from the rebound_at facts that reach it. Add the if/else and match cases to 74_uniq_flow.wf.

issues.finding: A reference to a nonportable value is portable: `&Rc` crosses fork branches (t02 rc_by_ref still accepted)
issues.description: props.rs eval and Lower::ty_has_in return false for Prop::Nonportable on Ty::Ref and Ty::Slice. A local `r = &n` with n: Rc, a tuple `(&n, 1)` and a parameter `r: &Rc<Node>` are all portable. Both fork branches can then clone the same Rc, which is a non-atomic refcount race. This is the rc_by_ref function of redteam t02, a probe the task names for RT8. The implementer reports only t02 line 11. ADR 0007 says 'nonportable ... work so at any depth', but that is not true through references. A side effect: in inner_handle_deps the new early return `if !self.is_nonportable(ty)` makes the `Ty::Ref(_) => handle_deps` arm unreachable.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4diff/p/np1.wf: only `direct` gives W0401. by_ref (line 9), in_tuple (line 14) and par_ref (line 18) give nothing. Also redteam/t02_fork.wf line 17.
issues.suggested_fix: Let Prop::Nonportable pass through Ref and Slice in props::eval and ty_has_in. Then check that inner_handle_deps still reaches its Ref arm, or remove the early return for references. Add bad and clean fork cases to 71_closure_modes.wf, and correct the ADR 0007 sentence.

issues.finding: Unset place fields are tracked only for a struct literal bound directly to a local; nested and returned literals allow a read of an uninitialized self-reference
issues.description: Val.unset is consumed only in assign_local, for the literal's own place fields. A literal used as a field of another literal (Outer { f: Frame {..} }), a literal returned from a function (ADR 0007: 'A function can return a struct literal: it is built in place'), and a literal in a tuple all lose the unset list. `o.f.cur`, `mk().cur` and `t.0.cur` can then be read before any value is set. This reads an uninitialized reference.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4diff/p/imm1.wf: nested_unset (line 8), returned_unset (line 12), returned_outer_unset (line 16) and tuple_unset (line 24) give no W0304. The direct case `let f = Frame{..}; print(f.cur)` is caught.
issues.suggested_fix: Carry the unset fields as paths inside Val: prefix them when a literal becomes a field, tuple part or payload of another value. Put unset place fields in the callee result: a returned type with place fields gives no value for them unless the body sets them, or the signature states it. Otherwise reject a return of a literal with unset place fields. Add the cases to 73_immovable.wf.

issues.finding: Part holders never retire: quadratic facts and false W0301 after a part or the whole local gets a new value
issues.description: assign() adds a hidden holder var for each `w.x = &...`. use_local and held_refs make each later use of w use every holder created so far, and the holders never go away. This has two effects. (1) Facts grow quadratically: 1000 part assignments give 1,003,001 `uses` facts against 3,001 on base, and 2000 assignments take 29.5 s against 0.23 s. (2) Stale holders keep old places: `w.x = &a[0]; w.x = &b[0]; a.clear(); print(w.x)` gives a false W0301, and so does a whole reassign `w = Wrap { x: &b[0] }`. Base gives no error for either. The flow-insensitive points_into imprecision in ADR 0003 covers whole locals, but the new holders could be strong-updated.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4diff/p/holders1000.wf and holders2000.wf (time, and `weft facts holders1000.wf f | grep -c ^uses`). For the false W0301: SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4diff/p/ref2.wf reassign_part_ok (line 10) and reassign_whole_ok (line 17).
issues.suggested_fix: Key part_holders by (local, place). A new value of the same place, or of the whole local (assign_local), replaces or retires the older holders. Uses then add only the live holders. Add a perf regression test like props::tests::a_wide_recursive_type_is_fast, and the two clean cases to 76_ref_flow.wf.

issues.finding: Quadratic Lower::finish: local_has -> var_has scans every local for every local and property
issues.description: finish calls local_has(i, p) 4 times per local. var_has does `self.locals.iter().filter(|l| l.var == v)`, so each call is O(L), and the inference loop runs it again for each lowering. The QR7/QR8 goal was to remove type-walk blow-ups, but this adds an O(L^2) step for long functions. A gdb sample confirms the hot path: finish -> local_has -> var_has. closure_uniq, is_copy_var and held_refs do the same linear scans.
issues.repro: Debug builds of base 353099e and head 3b1df44: SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4diff/p/locals5000.wf takes 3.3 s on head and 0.25 s on base. SCRATCH/verify/long_explain.wf (20 000 lines) takes 65.7 s on head and 2.2 s on base. le_10000.wf takes 12.0 s on head and 0.94 s on base.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep a VarId -> local index map, or a field var_local: Vec<Option<usize>>, in Lower. Use it in var_has, closure_uniq and is_copy_var. Or compute the flags once per local in finish without the per-var scan. Add a perf test with a few thousand locals.

issues.finding: A once closure loses its once-ness across a function boundary: returned or passed through, then called twice
issues.description: Once-ness lives only in the closure summary of the current body. A closure that a function item returns, or that a callee returns again (identity or pass-through), arrives as a plain fn() with no summary, so it is `many`. Two calls move the captured String twice. This is an RT8 shape ('a closure's mode follows from its captures') that is still open, and the ADRs do not record it.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4diff/p/ret1.wf twice_returned (line 12): `fn mk() -> fn() { let s = "abc"\n || eat(s) }`, then `let g = mk(); g(); g()` gives no W0502. SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4diff/p/ret2.wf: `fn mk(s: String) -> fn() { || eat(s) }` called twice, and `pass_through(|| eat(s))` called twice, give no error.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a `once` result part to the inferred signature (the body knows whether the returned closure is once), as `repeats` and `drops` are inferred. For pass-through callees, treat a fn result whose value can come from a once argument as once. Otherwise record the gap in ADR 0007 under the open items.

issues.finding: Linear temporaries held while a later argument, part or field aborts are not checked (F5/L2 shape)
issues.description: A linear temporary evaluated before a later operand that can abort has no variable with live_linear, so W0602 never fires. If the later operand aborts, the earlier Tok (which has no `on abort`) leaks. Base also misses this. It is the same 'linear values can leak across an abort' family as F5, and S4 changed the related tuple/compound logic.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4diff/p/abort2.wf: `spend_pair(mint(), risky_tok())` (line 10), `let p = (mint(), risky_tok())` (line 13) and `Two { a: mint(), b: risky_tok() }` (line 20) give no W0602.
issues.suggested_fix: When an operand is linear and later operands follow (hold_later already exists for references), bind it to a hidden linear var at its node and move it at the consuming node. live_linear and abort_unhandled then cover the window. Add the shapes to 70_type_props.wf.

issues.finding: `drops` gives W0601 for a generic Option<T> consumer that has a None arm
issues.description: fn opt_take<T>(o: Option<T>, f: fn(T)) { match o { Some(x) => f(x), None => {} } } has drops = {0}, so `opt_take(Some(begin()), rollback)` is W0601. ADR 0007 records this imprecision, but it is a common shape, and match_drops already consumes a local scrutinee in a None arm for concrete linear types.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4diff/p/lin2.wf line 30 (new in head; base gives nothing there).
issues.suggested_fix: In param_drops, count an arm that matches a constructor whose payload has no T part (pattern_holds_linear with T as maybe-linear) as a consume of the param.

issues.finding: W0301 text for a part holder reads 'the w.x used after it was invalidated'
issues.description: The hidden holder is VarKind::Temp and is named with the place text, and diagnose.rs formats Temp as `the {name}`.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4diff/p/ref2.wf line 24 (loop_holder).
issues.suggested_fix: Give holders their own kind or a name such as 'the value of `w.x`', or show them as `w.x`.

issues.finding: ADR and architecture gaps for the new rules
issues.description: (1) ADR 0007 lists 'A Vec of linear values is linear, and nothing consumes it: it is W0601 at its end' under 'What stays open (not checked)'. It is an over-rejection: every local Vec of linear values is W0601 even after all elements are popped (70_type_props multi_vec). It belongs under 'imprecise'. (2) No ADR records the definite-assignment semantics of `let x: T` (W0304): a capture by a closure or a clause counts as a use, also for an assignment inside the closure, and compound assignment reads. (3) The relation diagram in docs/architecture.md does not show overwrites, unset_at or use_before_set.
issues.repro: grep -rn W0304 docs/ finds only the place-field lines in ADR 0007.
issues.suggested_fix: Move the Vec item to the imprecise list. Add a W0304 bullet to ADR 0002 or 0007. Update the architecture diagram.

issues.finding: Lowering-time type decisions still miss values whose type the body resolves later
issues.description: finish recomputes the VarInfo flags, but wild_drops, drop_value, keep_modes and match_drops decide during lowering with the type known at that moment. `let v = Vec.new(); let _ = v.pop(); v.push(begin())` drops the popped Option<Tx> with no W0601.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4diff/p/late1.wf line 15.
issues.suggested_fix: Record pending drop sites with their type and the span, and decide linearity in finish from the resolved type, as check_int_lits does for literals.

issues.finding: A closure that returns a linear value is flagged inside its body (pre-existing, RT14 area)
issues.description: `let f = || begin(); let t = f(); rollback(t)` gives W0601 at the closure body `begin()`. The closure's tail value is treated as a dropped temporary. This is the same on base, but it falls in the RT14 area this stage worked on, and it rejects a correct program.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/partb/S4diff/p/lin2.wf lines 8 and 13.
issues.suggested_fix: Treat the tail value of a closure body as returned (moved to the closure result), not as a statement temporary.

issues.finding: ASD-STE100 and lint hygiene in new comments
issues.description: Several new comments have sentences of 26 to 36 words, for example props.rs ty_caps and recursive_adts, drops.rs keep_modes and match_drops, exhaust.rs specialize, repeat.rs give_fn, and stmt.rs finish and assign. `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` on call_flows has no comment that gives the reason.
issues.repro: git diff 353099e..HEAD -- crates/ | grep '^+.*//'
issues.suggested_fix: Split the sentences to 20 to 25 words or fewer. Add a one-line reason to the allow, or pass a small struct.

confirmed_fixed: RT8 main shapes: a linear closure that is never called (W0601), a once closure given to a callee that calls it twice, also through a fn value (W0502), a nested once closure, resume inside a closure (e02 W0502), an Rc captured by a closure and then forked (t02 line 11 W0401), a uniq capture across multi (e07)

Unannotated Vec flags recomputed in Lower::finish (bare_vec, multi_vec, corpus 70)

RT15: !Move through a struct field, a tuple, an array, Option and Vec push (W0604); W0605 for a self-reference assigned from another frame, a parameter, a local or a generic result, and for a struct literal; W0304 for a direct local literal with an unset place field

Eight majors remain:

2. The Local.uniq flag depends on lowering order across if/else and match. An aliased reference reaches an @ uniq parameter.

8. Linear temporaries held while a later operand aborts are not checked (W0602).

Minors:
- A documented false W0601 for Option<T> in `drops`.
- A diagnostic text glitch for part holders.
- The ADR lists the Vec-of-linear item under the wrong heading, W0304 semantics are not recorded, and the architecture diagram is not updated.
- Drop decisions at lowering time use the type known then, so a value whose type the body resolves later can drop silently.
- A false W0601 for a closure that returns a linear value. This was there before S4.
- Long sentences in comments, and an allow with no reason.

I fixed every real blocker and major from the S4 verification of review/s3 (/home/user/wt-core) and most of the minors, in two commits on top of 3b1df44: 45f4ca9 for code and tests, and ca3007a for docs. Head is ca3007a.

I reproduced each finding first, with the verifier probes and the old head binary.

**How the main fixes work:**
- **Generic drops:** a generic body now treats a value of a type parameter as possibly linear. `finish` runs the W0601 dataflow over these values, and their type parameters become the `drops` signature part. Callers check the inferred type argument.
- **Values on their way:** an operand that moves before the node that takes it gets a hidden holder. This fixes a false W0302 that S4 introduced, and gives W0602 when a later operand aborts.
- **Branch values:** the value of an `if` or `match` branch now moves, as in the interpreter.
- **Late types:** a move of a value whose type is not known yet is tentative, and `finish` settles it. Flags of hidden variables are set from the inferred type.
- **Modes in places:** nonportable and not-`many` marks go with a closure into fields, `Vec<fn()>`, tuples and `Option`, and into call results. A reference to a nonportable value is now nonportable.
- **W0304:** unset place fields come from the type of any freshly built value. A closure counts as reading the fields that its body reads.
- **Per-branch state:** `@ uniq` and part holders are joined at if/match and at loop exits, including `break` and `continue`. Part holders now retire, so they no longer give stale W0301s or quadratic facts.
- **W0120:** the check stops early on wildcard rows, and a match too large to check is now reported.
- **Speed:** locals are found by index (vars, roots, frames, names), so long bodies lower in linear time.

**Tests:** each fix has bad and clean cases in tests/programs 71–77 and in a new 78_closure_returns.wf (none has main or test blocks). Other new tests are in crates/weft-check/tests/body_texts.rs and crates/weft-sema/src/tests.rs (match budget, and a performance test with 12 000 lets).
